story: 天 can mean sky or day, depending on the word. In 天空, it refers to the sky above us. You also meet 天 when counting days, as in 一天, one day.
hint: Use 天空 to describe the sky above.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 天: sky

story: We walk firmly on the solid surface beneath our feet every day. Farmers work hard to plant seeds in the rich, dark layers of the earth. The word 土地 refers to the land or soil.
hint: Use 土地 to talk about land or ground.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 地: ground

story: 土 refers to soil or earth, the material in which plants grow. 泥土 means soil or mud. This word helps you describe what you find in a garden or on the ground.
hint: Use 泥土 to describe soil or dirt.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 土: soil

story: 石 means stone or rock. 石头 is the common everyday word for a stone, whether it is a small pebble or a larger piece of rock. You can use it when describing a path or a garden.
hint: Use 石头 to refer to a stone.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 石: stone

story: I walked along the beach and felt the soft sand under my feet. The children were busy building a large castle near the water. The word 沙子 refers to the tiny grains of sand found on the shore.
hint: Use 沙子 to describe the physical material of sand.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 沙: sand

story: 云 means cloud in modern simplified Chinese. 白云 means white cloud, combining a color with the thing it describes. It is a useful word when looking at the sky or talking about the weather.
hint: 白云 is the standard way to say white cloud.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 云: cloud

story: Dark clouds gathered quickly and soon it started to pour outside. I forgot my umbrella, so I had to run home to stay dry. We say 下雨 when it is raining.
hint: 下雨 is the common verb phrase for raining.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 雨: rain

story: The temperature dropped suddenly during the night while we were sleeping. When we woke up, the ground was covered in a thick layer of white. We use 下雪 to describe the action of snowing.
hint: Use 下雪 to talk about the weather snowing.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 雪: snow

story: The weather report says it will be very windy today. You should hold onto your hat when you walk outside. The phrase 大风 describes a strong wind that makes it difficult to walk comfortably in the open.
hint: Use with adjectives like big to describe strong wind.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 风: wind

story: Dark clouds gathered quickly in the afternoon sky. Suddenly, a loud sound echoed across the valley as the storm began. We use the phrase 打雷 to describe the action of thunder occurring during a heavy rainstorm.
hint: Describes the sound of a storm.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 雷: thunder

story: Modern homes rely on a steady supply of power to function properly. When the sun sets, we flip a switch to brighten the room. The term 电灯 refers to an electric light that illuminates our living spaces.
hint: Used for power and light devices.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 电: electricity

story: 气 can refer to air, breath, or gas, depending on the word. 空气 means air, the substance all around us. Start with this everyday word before exploring the character’s other uses.
hint: Refers to the atmosphere or breath.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 气: air

story: During a hot summer day, you might want a cold drink to cool down. You can add ice to your glass to make the liquid refreshing. In Chinese, we call this ice water, or 冰水, which is perfect for staying cool.
hint: Use this word when ordering cold drinks or describing frozen water.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 冰: ice

story: A river flows through the countryside, providing water for the nearby fields and trees. When you see a small stream of water moving through the land, you can call it a small river, or 小河, in Chinese.
hint: Refers to a natural flowing body of water like a stream.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 河: river

story: The vast blue ocean stretches as far as the eye can see under the bright sun. People love to visit the beach to look at the big sea, known as 大海 in Chinese, and listen to the waves crashing.
hint: Describes the vast ocean or large saltwater bodies.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 海: sea

story: The Yangtze River is a very famous and long waterway that flows across the country. In Chinese, this specific large river is called 长江, which is an important landmark for travel and trade throughout the entire region.
hint: Used for major, long rivers like the Yangtze.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 江: large river

story: We went to the park to see the beautiful scenery by the shore. The calm surface of the lake reflected the blue sky perfectly. In the phrase 湖水, it refers specifically to the clear lake water found there.
hint: Use this word when describing large bodies of water in nature.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 湖: lake

story: 泉 refers to a natural spring, a place where water emerges from the ground. 泉水 means spring water. The word helps you describe the water itself rather than a river or a lake.
hint: Refers to water coming directly from a natural underground source.
visual: Fresh water flowing from a spring
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 泉: spring

story: The wind was blowing strongly across the surface of the pond today. We watched as each small ripple moved steadily toward the edge of the grass. The word 波浪 describes these visible waves moving on the water.
hint: Commonly used to describe the rhythmic movement of water surfaces.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 波: wave

story: We stood on the sandy beach and watched the ocean move with great power. The tall sea waves crashed against the rocks with a loud sound. The phrase 海浪 refers to these large, powerful sea waves.
hint: Used for large, forceful waves typically found in the ocean.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 浪: large wave

story: I walked through the park and saw many beautiful colors. Every plant had a bright flower blooming in the sun. A flower garden is called 花园 in Chinese.
hint: Use 花园 to describe a place full of flowers.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 花: flower

story: The ground in the park is covered in soft green plants. I sat down on the small grass to rest. In Chinese, we call this small grass 小草.
hint: 小草 refers to small blades of grass.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 草: grass

story: We visited a quiet forest where tall green stalks grow very high. The panda loves to eat the fresh bamboo. We call this plant 竹子.
hint: 竹子 is the standard word for bamboo.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 竹: bamboo

story: Autumn is here and the colors are changing on the trees. I picked up a brown tree leaf from the ground. We call this leaf 树叶.
hint: 树叶 is the common term for tree leaves.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 叶: leaf

story: There is a very tall plant standing in the middle of our yard. I like to sit under the big tree for shade. We call it 大树.
hint: 大树 means a big, tall tree.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 树: tree

story: 根 means root, the part of a plant usually found below the soil. 树根 means tree root. You can use this word when describing the parts of a tree, alongside its branches and leaves.
hint: 树根 refers to the roots of a tree.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 根: root

story: I climbed up to reach the high part of the plant. I held onto a strong tree branch to keep my balance. We call this part 树枝.
hint: 树枝 is the word for a tree branch.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 枝: branch

story: We went on a long hike far away from the noisy city. We walked deep into the dense forest where many trees grow. We call this 森林.
hint: 森林 describes a large, dense forest area.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 森: dense forest

story: The night sky is very dark and clear tonight. I looked up and saw every bright star shining above us. We call these stars 星星.
hint: 星星 is the word for stars in the sky.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 星: star

story: The morning sky is bright as the day begins. I feel the warm sunlight on my face when I go outside. We call this light 阳光.
hint: 阳光 refers to the light from the sun.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 光: light

story: 空 can mean empty, and it also appears in words about the sky or space. 天空 means sky. Remember this complete word when describing what you see above the trees or rooftops.
hint: Used in 天空 to describe the open sky.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 空: empty; sky

story: Flowers begin to bloom as the weather gets warmer. This is the time when nature wakes up after the cold. We call this season the spring, a time for new growth. In 春天 (chūn tiān), the meaning is “spring.”
hint: Used in 春天 to name the spring season.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 春: spring season

story: The sun shines brightly and the days are very long. People enjoy swimming and eating ice cream to stay cool. This hot season is known as the summer. In 夏天 (xià tiān), the meaning is “summer.”
hint: Used in 夏天 to name the summer season.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 夏: summer

story: The leaves turn yellow and fall gently to the ground. The air feels crisp and cool as the harvest begins. This season is called the autumn, a time of change. In 秋天 (qiū tiān), the meaning is “autumn.”
hint: Used in 秋天 to name the autumn season.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 秋: autumn

story: Snow covers the ground and everyone wears thick coats. The air is freezing and the nights are very long. This cold season is known as the winter. In 冬天 (dōng tiān), the meaning is “winter.”
hint: Used in 冬天 to name the winter season.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 冬: winter

story: You reach for a glass of water from the fridge. It feels very chilly against your hand. We describe this temperature as cold, like the water in the glass. In 冷水 (lěng shuǐ), the meaning is “cold water.”
hint: Used in 冷水 to describe cold water.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 冷: cold

story: The tea is steaming and you must wait for it to cool down. It is too high in temperature to drink right now. We describe this state as hot. In 热水 (rè shuǐ), the meaning is “hot water.”
hint: Used in 热水 to describe hot water.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 热: hot

story: The clouds have all disappeared and the sun is shining bright. It is a perfect day to go outside and play in the park. We call this a sunny day. In 晴天 (qíng tiān), the meaning is “sunny day.”
hint: Used in 晴天 to describe a sunny day.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 晴: clear weather

story: 阴 can describe shade or an overcast sky. 阴天 means a cloudy day, when clouds hide the sun. It makes a useful weather pair with 晴天, meaning a sunny or clear day.
hint: Used in 阴天 to describe a cloudy day.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 阴: overcast; shade

story: 阳 is associated with sunlight and the sunny side of a place. In 太阳, the complete word means sun. This is the everyday word to use when talking about the sun in the sky.
hint: Used in 太阳 to name the sun.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 阳: sunny side

story: The morning air is very cold today. A thick layer of white mist covers the entire park, making it hard to see the trees. This is called 大雾, which means thick fog.
hint: Use 大雾 to describe a day with very low visibility.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 雾: fog

story: Early in the morning, I walked through the garden. I noticed small water droplets on the green leaves. These are called 露水, which is the Chinese word for dew.
hint: 露水 refers to the water droplets found on plants at dawn.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 露: dew

story: The artist looked at the beautiful sunset with great focus. His intense gaze captured every color in the sky. We call this look 目光, which means gaze or eyesight.
hint: 目光 describes the direction or intensity of someone's look.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 目: eye

story: The little boy listened carefully to the music playing in the room. He used his ears to hear every soft note. In Chinese, we call the ear 耳朵.
hint: 耳朵 is the standard term for the human ear.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 耳: ear

story: 手 means hand. 双手 means both hands, referring to the two hands together rather than a particular action. You can use this word when describing holding, carrying, or making something with both hands.
hint: 双手 is used when referring to using two hands together.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 手: hand

story: 足 can mean foot, as in 足球, football: a game played mainly with the feet. In other words, 足 can also mean enough. For this card, start by connecting it with feet and football.
hint: 足球 is the common name for the sport of football.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 足: foot; enough

story: 头 means head, and it also appears in the word 头发, meaning hair. In this everyday word, 发 names the hair and 头 tells you where it grows. Learn 头发 together as one word.
hint: 头发 specifically refers to the hair on one's head.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 头: head

story: 心 means heart, but it also appears in expressions about thoughts and care. 小心 means be careful. You may hear this short warning when someone wants you to watch your step or handle something carefully.
hint: 小心 is a common phrase for being cautious or careful.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 心: heart

story: After running for an hour, he felt very tired. He sat down to rest and relax his whole body. We call the body 身体 in Chinese.
hint: 身体 refers to the physical body of a person.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 身: body

story: 牙 refers to a tooth or teeth. The everyday word 牙齿 means teeth. You might hear it when someone talks about brushing their teeth or visiting a dentist.
hint: 牙齿 is the standard word for teeth.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 牙: tooth

story: The tongue is essential for tasting delicious food and speaking clearly. When you eat, your tongue helps move food around your mouth. In the phrase 舌头, it refers to the tongue itself.
hint: Use 舌头 to talk about the tongue in your mouth.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 舌: tongue

story: Your nose helps you breathe and smell the fresh air outside. It is located right in the middle of your face. The word 鼻子 is the common term used for a nose.
hint: 鼻子 is the standard word for your nose.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 鼻: nose

story: Every morning, you wash your face to feel refreshed and clean. Your face shows your expressions to the people you meet. The phrase 洗脸 means to wash the face.
hint: 洗脸 is the action of washing your face.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 脸: face

story: 眼 refers to an eye. In everyday conversation, 眼睛 is the usual word for eyes. You can use it when describing someone’s eyes or talking about what you can see.
hint: 眼睛 is the common word for eyes.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 眼: eye

story: Here, 发 is read fà and means hair. The word 头发 refers to the hair on your head. This same written character can also be read fā with other meanings, so remember the word and pronunciation together.
hint: 头发 is the word for hair on the head.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 发: hair

story: 毛 means hair or fur, including the soft covering on an animal. You also meet it in 毛巾, meaning towel. Learn 毛巾 as a complete everyday word for something you use after washing.
hint: 毛巾 is a towel used for drying.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 毛: hair; fur

story: 皮 can mean skin or the outer covering of something. 皮肤 specifically refers to human skin. The complete word helps you distinguish this meaning from other uses, such as the skin of a fruit.
hint: 皮肤 is the word for human skin.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 皮: skin

story: 血 means blood and is read xuè on this card. 血液 is a common word for blood. Remember the complete word and its pronunciation together when learning vocabulary about the body.
hint: 血液 is the formal word for blood.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 血: blood

story: Your body has a strong frame made of many pieces. These parts support your weight and help you move around. The word 骨头 refers to a bone in the body.
hint: 骨头 is the word for a bone.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 骨: bone

story: 男 refers to being male. 男孩 means boy: 男 identifies a male child, while 孩 relates to a child. It pairs naturally with 女孩, girl, when learning words for people.
hint: 男孩 is the word for a boy.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 男: male

story: 女 refers to being female. 女孩 means girl, while 男孩 means boy. Learning these words together helps you recognize how Chinese names different members of a family or group.
hint: Used to describe female people, as seen in the word for girl.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 女: female

story: Every afternoon, the park is full of energy and noise. You can see a happy child playing on the swings with their friends. The word 孩子 means child, referring to a young human.
hint: Refers to a young person, used in the word for child.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 子: child

story: The teacher greeted every student as they entered the classroom this morning. She cares deeply about each small child in her care. The word 小孩 means child, describing a young boy or girl.
hint: Used specifically in the compound word for a small child.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 孩: child

story: 父 refers to a father and is common in more formal family words. 父亲 means father. In everyday conversation, people also use 爸爸, dad, especially when speaking directly to their own father.
hint: Formal term for a male parent, used in the word father.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 父: father

story: 母 refers to a mother and appears in the word 母亲, meaning mother. For everyday speech, 妈妈 is another common word. Learn 母亲 alongside 父亲, father, as a useful family pair.
hint: Formal term for a female parent, used in the word mother.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 母: mother

story: On weekends, we often go to the park to play catch together. My dad is very funny and tells the best stories. The word 爸爸 means dad, an informal term for a father.
hint: Informal term for father, used in the word dad.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 爸: dad

story: She always knows exactly what to say when I am feeling sad. My mum is very supportive and kind to everyone. The word 妈妈 means mum, an informal term for a mother.
hint: Informal term for mother, used in the word mum.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 妈: mum

story: He always helps me with my homework when I get stuck on difficult problems. My elder brother is very smart and patient. The word 兄弟 means brothers, referring to male siblings in a family.
hint: Refers to an older male sibling, used in the word brothers.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 兄: elder brother

story: We enjoy playing video games together after we finish our school work. My younger brother is very energetic and loves to run outside. The word 弟弟 means younger brother, a male sibling younger than you.
hint: Refers to a younger male sibling, used in the word brother.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 弟: younger brother

story: She taught me how to bake cookies when I was just a little kid. My elder sister is very talented and creative. The word 姐姐 means elder sister, a female sibling older than you.
hint: Refers to an older female sibling, used in the word sister.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 姐: elder sister

story: My younger sister loves to read books in the afternoon. She is very kind and always shares her snacks with me. We call her 妹妹 when we talk about her at home.
hint: Use 妹妹 to refer to a younger sister.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 妹: younger sister

story: 友 means friend and is usually part of a longer word in everyday speech. 朋友 is the common word for a friend. Use the whole word when talking about someone you know and like.
hint: Part of the word 朋友 for friend.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 友: friend

story: You usually meet 朋 in 朋友, meaning friend. Learn the two characters together rather than using 朋 by itself. 我的朋友 means my friend, a simple phrase for introducing someone you know.
hint: Combine with 友 to mean friend.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 朋: friend

story: Our teacher is very patient and explains math problems clearly. She helps us learn new things every single day. We call her 老师 at school.
hint: Use 老师 to address a teacher.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 师: teacher

story: 生 has several common meanings connected with life, birth, and growing. In 学生, it refers to a student. Learn 学生 as a whole word: someone who studies at school is a 学生.
hint: Use 学生 to describe a student.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 生: life; student

story: 我 means I or me, the person who is speaking. Add 们 to form 我们, meaning we or us. This lets you move from talking about yourself to talking about a group that includes you.
hint: Use 我 to say I or me.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 我: I; me

story: 你 means you, the person being spoken to. In 你好, it forms the familiar greeting hello. Say 你好 when meeting someone; it is a complete greeting rather than a question.
hint: Use 你好 to say hello.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 你: you

story: 他 means he or him. Adding 们 gives 他们, meaning they or them, usually for a male or mixed group. Compare it with 我们, we, to keep the different groups clear.
hint: Use 他们 for they or them.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 他: he; him

story: 她 means she or her and has the same pronunciation as 他, he. 她们 refers to a female group: they or them. The written characters distinguish meanings that sound the same in speech.
hint: Use 她们 for they or them (female).
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 她: she; her

story: The elderly person sits on the bench and watches the birds fly. He has many interesting stories to tell about the past. We call him 老人.
hint: Use 老人 to refer to an elderly person.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 老: old

story: My friend is a very kind person. He always helps others when they are in trouble. We call him a good person because he has a warm heart. In 好人 (hǎo rén), the meaning is “good person.”
hint: Use with 'rén' to describe a kind person.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 好: good

story: She shows her love by helping the community every weekend. Her loving heart makes everyone feel welcome and happy. It is important to share kindness with others. In 爱心 (ài xīn), the meaning is “loving heart.”
hint: Use with 'xīn' to describe a kind heart.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 爱: love

story: The children play in the park and laugh loudly together. Their happy faces show how much fun they are having today. It is wonderful to hear them laugh. In 大笑 (dà xiào), the meaning is “laugh loudly.”
hint: Use with 'dà' to describe loud laughter.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 笑: laugh; smile

story: The baby woke up and started to cry because he was hungry. I heard the sound of crying and went to check on him. He stopped once he was fed. In 哭声 (kū shēng), the meaning is “sound of crying.”
hint: Use with 'shēng' to describe the sound of crying.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 哭: cry

story: I like to sit in the library and read a book quietly. When I look at the pages, I learn many new things. It is a great way to spend time. In 看书 (kàn shū), the meaning is “read a book.”
hint: Use with 'shū' to describe reading a book.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 看: look; watch

story: I heard that the weather will be sunny tomorrow. I am happy to hear that news from my friend. We plan to go for a walk outside. In 听说 (tīng shuō), the meaning is “hear that.”
hint: Use with 'shuō' to mean 'I heard that'.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 听: listen

story: We sit together and speak about our plans for the weekend. It is nice to speak with friends after a long day of work. We enjoy sharing stories. In 说话 (shuō huà), the meaning is “speak.”
hint: Use with 'huà' to describe the act of speaking.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 说: speak

story: Every day, I go to the classroom to study new topics. I enjoy the process of study because it helps me grow. I want to learn more every year. In 学习 (xué xí), the meaning is “study.”
hint: Use with 'xí' to describe the act of studying.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 学: learn

story: 米 refers to rice grains, especially the uncooked rice used to prepare a meal. 大米 is a common word for rice. Compare it with 米饭, which specifically means cooked rice.
hint: Use with 'dà' to refer to rice as food.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 米: rice grains

story: For food, 面 is used for flour and noodles. A bowl of 面条 is a bowl of noodles, a familiar meal. The same written character also appears in words about faces, so the surrounding word matters.
hint: Use with 'tiáo' to describe a bowl of noodles.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 面: noodles; flour

story: 饭 can refer to cooked rice or to a meal more generally. 米饭 specifically means cooked rice, while 吃饭 means to eat a meal. These two everyday words help you recognize both uses.
hint: Use 米饭 to talk about cooked rice as a staple food.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 饭: cooked rice; meal

story: 菜 can mean a vegetable or a prepared dish. 白菜 means Chinese cabbage, a familiar vegetable. When talking about a meal, 菜 can also describe the dishes served alongside rice.
hint: Use 白菜 for the specific vegetable known as Chinese cabbage.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 菜: vegetable; dish

story: Every afternoon, I like to sit by the window and drink tea. The warm liquid helps me relax after a busy morning. It is a very popular drink here. In 喝茶 (hē chá), the meaning is “drink tea.”
hint: Use 喝茶 when you want to say drink tea.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 茶: tea

story: 奶 means milk. 牛奶 specifically means cow’s milk and is the everyday word often used on a milk carton. Recognizing 牛奶 is useful when shopping or ordering a drink.
hint: Use 牛奶 to refer specifically to cow's milk.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 奶: milk

story: The weather is cold outside today. I decide to make some hot soup for my family. We enjoy drinking soup together to stay warm and comfortable. In 喝汤 (hē tāng), the meaning is “drink soup.”
hint: Use 喝汤 to describe the action of drinking soup.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 汤: soup

story: We are preparing a big dinner for the weekend. I am going to cook some beef for everyone. Everyone loves eating meat when we have a special celebration. In 牛肉 (niú ròu), the meaning is “beef.”
hint: Use 牛肉 to specify beef in your meals.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 肉: meat

story: I went to the river to catch a small fish today. It was a fun experience for me. I brought it home to cook for my dinner tonight. In 小鱼 (xiǎo yú), the meaning is “small fish.”
hint: Use 小鱼 to describe a small fish.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 鱼: fish

story: 蛋 means egg. 鸡蛋 specifically means a chicken egg, combining the animal with the food. This is a useful word to recognize when shopping or reading a breakfast menu.
hint: Use 鸡蛋 to refer to a chicken egg.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 蛋: egg

story: It is a very hot summer day today. I bought a large watermelon to share with my friends. We enjoy eating this sweet melon to cool down. In 西瓜 (xī guā), the meaning is “watermelon.”
hint: Use 西瓜 to talk about watermelon.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 瓜: melon

story: 果 means fruit, and 水果 is the everyday general word for fruit. Apples, pears, and oranges are all 水果. Use the complete word when talking about buying or eating fruit.
hint: Use 水果 as a general term for fruit.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 果: fruit

story: 豆 refers to a bean. 豆子 is the everyday word for beans, which can be used in soups and many other dishes. Learn the whole word when naming food at a market.
hint: Use 豆子 to talk about beans in a meal.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 豆: bean

story: My friend brought me a box of colorful sweets from the shop. I love eating them because they taste very sugary and delicious. In Chinese, we call these sweets 糖果.
hint: Use 糖果 when referring to candy or sweets.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 糖: sugar; sweet

story: When I cook vegetables, I always add a little bit of salt to improve the flavor. It is important not to use too much. The term 食盐 is the standard word for table salt.
hint: Use 食盐 for the salt used in cooking.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 盐: salt

story: I need to pour some cooking oil into the pan before frying the eggs. This helps prevent the food from sticking to the surface. We call this cooking oil 食用油.
hint: Use 食用油 for oil used in cooking.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 油: oil

story: I enjoy having a cup of cold yoghurt for breakfast every morning. It has a slightly sour taste that I find very refreshing. The Chinese word for yoghurt is 酸奶.
hint: Use 酸奶 to order or describe yoghurt.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 酸: sour

story: I bought a sweet melon at the fruit stand because it looked very ripe. It was so juicy and tasted like honey. The Chinese word 甜瓜 describes this type of melon.
hint: Use 甜瓜 to describe a sweet melon.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 甜: sweet

story: 苦 describes a bitter taste, different from sweet or sour. 苦瓜 means bitter melon, a vegetable named for this taste. The word offers a familiar food example for remembering the meaning.
hint: Use 苦瓜 to refer to bitter melon.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 苦: bitter

story: I added a fresh chilli pepper to my noodles to make them spicy. It gave the dish a very strong and exciting flavor. The word 辣椒 is used for chilli peppers.
hint: Use 辣椒 to talk about spicy peppers.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 辣: spicy

story: The flowers in the garden have a very pleasant smell today. I love walking past them because the fragrance is so lovely. We use 香味 to describe this pleasant smell.
hint: Use 香味 to describe a good scent.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 香: fragrant

story: After eating a large bowl of rice, I finally feel full. It was a very satisfying meal that gave me plenty of energy. We use 吃饱 to say we have eaten until full.
hint: Use 吃饱 to express being full after eating.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 饱: full after eating

story: You skipped breakfast and lunch today because you were very busy. Now your stomach is making loud noises because you are hungry. You say you are hungry now to your friend. In 饿了 (è le), the meaning is “hungry now.”
hint: Use this to describe the feeling of needing food.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 饿: hungry

story: It is time for dinner after a long day of work. You sit down at the table with your family to eat a meal together. Everyone enjoys the delicious food. In 吃饭 (chī fàn), the meaning is “eat a meal.”
hint: Use this verb for consuming any type of food.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 吃: eat

story: After running in the park, you feel very thirsty from the heat. You go to the kitchen to drink water from a clean glass. It feels very refreshing. In 喝水 (hē shuǐ), the meaning is “drink water.”
hint: Use this verb for consuming liquids like water or tea.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 喝: drink

story: You put raw rice and water into a pot on the stove. You wait for the water to bubble so you can cook rice for dinner. It smells great. In 煮饭 (zhǔ fàn), the meaning is “cook rice.”
hint: Use this for preparing food by boiling in water.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 煮: boil; cook

story: You heat up a pan with a little bit of oil. You add fresh vegetables and stir-fry dishes quickly over high heat. This makes the vegetables taste very crunchy. In 炒菜 (chǎo cài), the meaning is “stir-fry dishes.”
hint: Use this for cooking food quickly in a pan.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 炒: stir-fry

story: 烧 can mean to burn or to heat something as part of cooking. 烧水 means to boil water. In this phrase, the action is heating water rather than burning the water itself.
hint: Use this for heating liquids or cooking with fire.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 烧: burn; cook

story: You invite your friends over for a weekend dinner party. You decide to roast meat in the oven until it is golden brown. Everyone loves the savory smell. In 烤肉 (kǎo ròu), the meaning is “roast meat.”
hint: Use this for cooking food using dry oven heat.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 烤: roast; bake

story: 蒸 means to cook with steam rather than placing food directly in water or oil. 蒸鱼 means to steam fish. It is one of several cooking words you may recognize on a menu.
hint: Use this for cooking food using hot steam.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 蒸: steam

story: You finish cooking a large pot of hot soup for everyone. You take a clean rice bowl from the cupboard to serve the food. It is the perfect size. In 饭碗 (fàn wǎn), the meaning is “rice bowl.”
hint: Use this noun for the container used for soup.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 碗: bowl

story: You are feeling thirsty while working at your desk. You reach for your favorite drinking cup and fill it with cold water. It helps you stay focused. In 水杯 (shuǐ bēi), the meaning is “drinking cup.”
hint: Use this noun for a container used for drinking.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 杯: cup

story: I place the hot food on a clean plate. It is very convenient for serving dinner to my family. We always wash the plate after we finish eating our meal. In 盘子 (pán zi), the meaning is “plate.”
hint: Use this word when talking about the dishware for serving food.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 盘: plate

story: I use a pair of chopsticks to pick up my noodles. They are very useful for eating Asian food. My friend is learning how to hold chopsticks correctly today. In 筷子 (kuài zi), the meaning is “chopsticks.”
hint: Commonly used in the compound 筷子 for the eating utensil.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 筷: chopstick

story: I use a small spoon to stir sugar into my coffee. It helps me mix the drink well. I also use a large spoon to serve soup from the pot. In 勺子 (sháo zi), the meaning is “spoon.”
hint: Used in the compound 勺子 to refer to a spoon.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 勺: spoon

story: The chef uses a sharp kitchen knife to cut fresh vegetables. It makes cooking much faster and easier. Please be careful when you use a knife in the kitchen. In 菜刀 (cài dāo), the meaning is “kitchen knife.”
hint: Used in the compound 菜刀 for a kitchen knife.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 刀: knife

story: 餐 refers to a meal. 早餐 means breakfast, the meal eaten in the morning. You will also meet 餐 in words for other meals and places where people eat.
hint: Used in the compound 早餐 to mean breakfast.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 餐: meal

story: 饼 refers to several kinds of flat cakes or breads. In 饼干, the complete word means biscuit or cookie. Remember 饼干 as the familiar snack rather than translating the two characters separately.
hint: Used in the compound 饼干 to mean biscuit or cookie.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 饼: flat cake

story: We are having roasted chicken meat for dinner tonight. It is a very popular dish in my house. Everyone enjoys eating chicken because it tastes delicious. In 鸡肉 (jī ròu), the meaning is “chicken meat.”
hint: Used in the compound 鸡肉 to refer to chicken meat.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 鸡: chicken

story: I saw a cute duck swimming in the park pond today. It was moving very fast in the water. Many people enjoy eating duck at special restaurants. In 鸭子 (yā zi), the meaning is “duck.”
hint: Used in the compound 鸭子 to refer to a duck.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 鸭: duck

story: The farmer raises a big cow on his green farm. It provides fresh milk every day. We also buy beef at the market to cook for our dinner. In 牛肉 (niú ròu), the meaning is “beef.”
hint: Used in the compound 牛肉 to refer to beef.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 牛: cow

story: The little sheep is eating grass in the field. It has soft white wool. We often buy mutton at the butcher shop to make a warm stew. In 羊肉 (yáng ròu), the meaning is “mutton.”
hint: Used in the compound 羊肉 to refer to mutton.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 羊: sheep

story: The farmer keeps a large pig in the barn. He feeds it every morning before starting his work. The term 猪肉 refers to pork, which is a very common ingredient in many delicious home-cooked meals.
hint: Use 猪肉 to talk about pork in a restaurant or market.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 猪: pig

story: We went to the seafood market to buy fresh shrimp for dinner. My father loves to cook them with garlic and soy sauce. A large shrimp is called 大虾 in Chinese cooking.
hint: Use 大虾 to describe a large-sized shrimp.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 虾: shrimp

story: 蟹 means crab, a sea or freshwater animal with a hard shell and claws. 螃蟹 is the usual everyday word. You may see this word at a seafood market or on a menu.
hint: Use 螃蟹 to refer to a crab.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 蟹: crab

story: The garden is full of trees that bloom in the spring. By summer, we can pick a sweet peach to eat as a snack. We call this fruit 桃子 in everyday conversation.
hint: Use 桃子 when buying or eating a peach.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 桃: peach

story: I keep a bowl of fruit on the kitchen table for everyone. My favorite snack is a crisp, juicy pear after lunch. In Chinese, we call this fruit 梨子.
hint: Use 梨子 to refer to a pear.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 梨: pear

story: Learn 苹 together with 果 in 苹果, the everyday word for apple. It is usually this complete word that you need when naming or buying the fruit. A single apple is 一个苹果.
hint: Use 苹果 to talk about an apple.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 苹: apple (in 苹果)

story: The fruit bowl is bright and colorful today. I decided to peel a fresh orange to make some juice. We call this citrus fruit 橙子 in our daily life.
hint: Use 橙子 to refer to an orange.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 橙: orange

story: 饺 is normally learned in the word 饺子, meaning dumpling. You can use 吃饺子 when talking about eating dumplings. Remember the complete word rather than trying to use 饺 alone in conversation.
hint: Use 饺子 to order or describe a dumpling.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 饺: dumpling (in 饺子)

story: After a long day of work, I look forward to relaxing in my living room. It feels wonderful to finally return to my residence. We use 回家 to mean going home.
hint: Use 回家 to say you are going home.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 家: home; family

story: I arrived at the office early this morning. I reached into my bag to find my key so I could enter the building. I need to 开门 to open the door.
hint: Use 开门 to ask someone to open the door.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 门: door

story: I look outside to see the garden through the glass. The fresh air enters whenever I open the window. In Chinese, we call this a 窗户, which simply means a window.
hint: Use 窗户 for window in daily conversation.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 窗: window

story: My new apartment has plenty of space for my things. I spend most of my time relaxing in my bedroom. We use the word 房间 to describe a room in a house.
hint: 房间 refers to a specific room.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 房: room; house

story: 屋 means house or a room within a building. 屋子 is a common word for a house or room, depending on context. Use the surrounding sentence to understand which place is being described.
hint: 屋子 is a common word for house.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 屋: house

story: Students sit at their desks to listen to the teacher. The air is quiet as everyone focuses on their studies. We call this place a 教室, meaning a classroom.
hint: 教室 is the standard word for classroom.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 室: room

story: After a long day, I like to sit on the sofa to watch television. The family gathers here to talk and relax together. We call this area a 客厅, the living room.
hint: 客厅 is the living room area.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 厅: hall

story: I feel very tired after working all day long. It is finally time to rest and get some sleep. We say 上床 when we go to bed at night.
hint: 上床 means to go to bed.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 床: bed

story: I place my laptop and coffee on the flat surface to work. It is sturdy enough to hold all my office supplies. We call this piece of furniture a 桌子, a table.
hint: 桌子 is the word for table.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 桌: table

story: 椅 refers to a chair, a seat usually made for one person. 椅子 is the complete everyday word. Learn it together with 桌子, table, for two familiar pieces of furniture.
hint: 椅子 is the word for chair.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 椅: chair

story: When the sun goes down, the room becomes very dark. I flip the switch to turn on the bright light. We call this device an 电灯, an electric light.
hint: 电灯 refers to an electric light.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 灯: lamp

story: I enjoy reading stories about adventures in distant lands. I keep my collection neatly arranged on the wooden shelf. We call these items 书本, which means books.
hint: 书本 is the word for books.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 书: book

story: I use a pen to write my daily notes in my notebook. It is very smooth and easy to hold. The term 毛笔 refers to a traditional writing brush used for calligraphy.
hint: Used for writing; 毛笔 is a traditional brush.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 笔: pen

story: I need to buy some paper to print my homework for class tomorrow. I prefer using high-quality sheets for my essays. The phrase 白纸 means plain white paper.
hint: Material for writing; 白纸 is white paper.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 纸: paper

story: I put my heavy books inside my bag before leaving for school. It helps me carry everything I need for the day. The word 书包 means a schoolbag.
hint: Container for items; 书包 is a schoolbag.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 包: bag

story: I choose comfortable clothing to wear when I go out with my friends on weekends. It is important to dress for the weather. The word 衣服 means clothes.
hint: Garments worn; 衣服 means clothes.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 衣: clothing

story: I always tie my shoelaces tightly before I go for a run in the park. Good footwear makes exercise much more enjoyable. The term 鞋子 means shoes.
hint: Footwear; 鞋子 means shoes.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 鞋: shoe

story: 车 is a broad word for a vehicle. 汽车 specifically means car, while other words name different vehicles. Recognizing 车 helps you begin to understand common words about travel and transport.
hint: Mode of transport; 汽车 means a car.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 车: vehicle

story: In the old movies, people often traveled across the countryside using a horse. It was a common sight in rural areas long ago. The term 马车 means a horse-drawn cart.
hint: Animal used for riding; 马车 is a carriage.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 马: horse

story: We walked along the main road to reach the shopping center in the city. There were many people walking and driving nearby. The term 马路 means a road.
hint: Path for travel; 马路 is a road.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 路: road

story: There are many interesting shops located on the main street near my apartment. I enjoy walking there to look at the displays. The term 大街 means a main street.
hint: Public thoroughfare; 大街 is a main street.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 街: street

story: We crossed the large bridge to get to the other side of the river. The view from the top was beautiful and very wide. The term 大桥 means a large bridge.
hint: Structure over water; 大桥 is a large bridge.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 桥: bridge

story: I walked into the local shop to buy some snacks for my trip. The clerk was very friendly and helped me find everything I needed quickly. In the example, 书店 refers to a bookshop where you can buy books.
hint: Used for places where you buy goods or stay.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 店: shop

story: The city is very busy during the day with many people walking around. There are tall buildings and many shops everywhere you look. In the example, 城市 means city, describing a large urban area.
hint: Refers to a city or a market area.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 市: city; market

story: My friend traveled to a different country to learn about its unique culture and history. She enjoyed meeting new people and trying local food. In the example, 中国 refers to the country of China.
hint: Used to describe a nation or country.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 国: country

story: The old city has beautiful walls that were built many years ago to protect the people. Today, it is a popular place for tourists to visit. In the example, 城市 means city, referring to an urban center.
hint: Refers to a city or a walled area.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 城: city

story: 村 means village, a settlement smaller than a town or city. 村子 is a common everyday word for a village. It helps you describe where someone lives or a place you visit.
hint: Used for a small rural settlement.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 村: village

story: 校 appears in 学校, the everyday word for school. It is read xiào in this word. When you talk about going to school, 去学校 is a simple phrase to recognize and practise.
hint: Used in words related to education.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 校: school (in 学校)

story: 院 can refer to a courtyard or appear in names of institutions. In 医院, the complete word means hospital. Remember 医院 as a place name rather than translating each character separately.
hint: Used for institutions or courtyards.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 院: courtyard; institution

story: I waited at the bus station for my ride to arrive on time. It was a busy place with many people coming and going all day. In the example, 车站 means a bus or train station.
hint: Used for transit stops or standing.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 站: station; stand

story: 机 is used in words for machines and devices. In 飞机, it helps name an airplane. Learn 飞机 as a complete word you can recognize when talking about travel or visiting an airport.
hint: Used for machines or mechanical devices.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 机: machine

story: 场 can refer to an open area or a place used for an activity. In 机场, it helps name an airport. The whole word tells you the place where airplanes arrive and leave.
hint: Used for open areas or venues.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 场: open area; venue

story: The family decided to take a trip across the lake. They boarded a small boat to enjoy the calm water. It was a peaceful afternoon for everyone. In 小船 (xiǎo chuán), the meaning is “small boat.”
hint: Use this for water transport like a small boat.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 船: boat

story: The large ship arrived at the busy harbour early this morning. Many workers were waiting to unload the heavy cargo. It is a very important place for trade. In 港口 (gǎng kǒu), the meaning is “harbour.”
hint: Refers to a harbour or port area.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 港: harbour

story: We took a long flight to reach the beautiful island. The beach was quiet and the sand was very white. We loved staying on that small island. In 小岛 (xiǎo dǎo), the meaning is “small island.”
hint: Used for land surrounded by water.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 岛: island

story: Every Sunday, the family goes to the local park to play. The children run on the grass while the parents sit on a bench. It is a lovely public space. In 公园 (gōng yuán), the meaning is “park.”
hint: Refers to a garden or public park.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 园: garden; park

story: 公 often refers to something public or shared. In 公共, it expresses the idea of public use. You will meet this word when reading about shared places, public services, and things available to everyone.
hint: Means public or shared by everyone.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 公: public

story: He starts his work at eight o'clock every single morning. He enjoys his job because he learns something new every day. He is very happy with his career. In 工作 (gōng zuò), the meaning is “work.”
hint: Refers to work or a job.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 工: work

story: The new factory produces many items for people to buy. It is located just outside the city near the main road. Many people have jobs there. In 工厂 (gōng chǎng), the meaning is “factory.”
hint: Refers to a factory or industrial building.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 厂: factory

story: They live in a very tall building in the center of town. Their apartment is on the tenth floor. The view from the window is truly amazing. In 高楼 (gāo lóu), the meaning is “tall building.”
hint: Refers to a building or a floor.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 楼: building; floor

story: He walked up the stairs to reach the second floor of the house. The wooden steps were very sturdy and safe to use. He arrived at the top quickly. In 楼梯 (lóu tī), the meaning is “stairs.”
hint: Refers to stairs or a ladder.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 梯: stairs; ladder

story: The artist painted a beautiful picture on the wall of the room. It made the whole house look much brighter and more colorful. Everyone liked the new design. In 墙上 (qiáng shàng), the meaning is “on the wall.”
hint: Refers to a wall in a room.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 墙: wall

story: I like to walk in the park every morning to enjoy the fresh air. It is a great way to start my day. In Chinese, we use the word 走路 to describe the act of walking.
hint: Use 走路 to talk about the action of walking.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 走: walk

story: My dog loves to run fast when we play at the beach. He is very energetic and never gets tired. We use the word 跑步 to describe this fast running activity.
hint: Use 跑步 to describe the sport or action of running.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 跑: run

story: I went to the store to buy some milk this afternoon. Now I am ready to come back home to rest. We use the word 回来 to mean coming back.
hint: Use 回来 to express the action of returning or coming back.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 来: come

story: The weather is sunny today, so I want to go out for a walk. It is nice to get some sunshine. We use the word 出去 to mean going out.
hint: Use 出去 to describe the action of going outside.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 去: go

story: After a long day at the office, I am happy to go home. I look forward to relaxing in my favorite chair. We use the word 回家 to mean going home.
hint: Use 回家 to talk about returning to your home.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 回: return

story: When I arrive at my house, I need to open the door to get inside. It is heavy, so I use both hands. We use the word 开门 to mean opening the door.
hint: Use 开门 to describe the action of opening a door.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 开: open

story: Before I go to sleep, I always make sure to close the door for safety. It keeps the room quiet and private. We use the word 关门 to mean closing the door.
hint: Use 关门 to describe the action of closing a door.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 关: close

story: I am very tired after standing for a long time at the station. I see a bench and decide to sit down. We use the word 坐下 to mean sitting down.
hint: Use 坐下 to describe the action of sitting down.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 坐: sit

story: I went to the market and bought one apple for my snack. It was very sweet and fresh. We use the word 一个 to count one item of something.
hint: Use 一个 as a common way to count one object.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 一: one

story: My birthday is in the second month of the year. I always celebrate it with my family and friends. We use the word 二月 to refer to the month of February.
hint: Use 二月 to refer to the second month, February.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 二: two

story: I have three friends coming over to visit my house today. We plan to spend three days exploring the city together. The phrase 三天 means three days in total.
hint: Use 三 to count items or time periods like three days.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 三: three

story: 四 is the number four. In 四季, it counts the four seasons: spring, summer, autumn, and winter. Practise saying sì clearly so you can recognize it when counting or talking about a number.
hint: Use 四 to describe groups of four, such as four seasons.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 四: four

story: I went to the store and bought five apples for my lunch. My friend also wanted some, so I gave him five items from my bag. 五个 means five items.
hint: Use 五 followed by a measure word for five objects.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 五: five

story: 六 is the number six. In 六月, it names June, the sixth month of the year. Chinese month names follow this simple pattern: a number comes before 月.
hint: Use 六 before 月 to name the month of June.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 六: six

story: I am going on a trip for seven days to see the mountains. I have already packed my bags and checked the weather forecast. 七天 means seven days.
hint: Use 七 to count seven days or seven items.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 七: seven

story: 八 is the number eight. 八月 means August, the eighth month of the year. Recognizing the number and 月 together helps you read a calendar or understand someone’s travel plans.
hint: Use 八 before 月 to name the month of August.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 八: eight

story: 九 is the number nine. 九个 means nine items when the object being counted is understood. Practise saying jiǔ together with the other numbers from one to ten.
hint: Use 九 followed by a measure word for nine objects.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 九: nine

story: I have ten days of vacation left before I return to work. I plan to relax and enjoy the quiet time at home. 十天 means ten days.
hint: Use 十 to count ten days or ten items.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 十: ten

story: The library has a large collection of books for everyone to enjoy. I counted one hundred books on the history shelf alone. 一百 means one hundred.
hint: Use 百 to express quantities in the hundreds.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 百: hundred

story: The city park is very large and has many beautiful trees. I walked one thousand steps while enjoying the fresh air today. 一千 means one thousand.
hint: Use 千 to express quantities in the thousands.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 千: thousand

story: You are counting items in a large warehouse. You count ten thousand boxes stacked neatly on the shelves. The total number is一万, which means ten thousand.
hint: Used for large numbers like ten thousand.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 万: ten thousand

story: 零 is the number zero. 零个 means zero items or none of the things being counted. Notice that the measure word 个 follows the number, just as it does in 三个, three items.
hint: Used to represent zero or nothing.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 零: zero

story: 两 is commonly used for two before a measure word. 两个 means two items. Compare this with 二 in a number or a date: both express two, but they fit different everyday patterns.
hint: Used for the quantity of two.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 两: two (before a measure word)

story: 半 means half. 半天 literally means half a day, but it can also mean a long time in everyday speech. The surrounding sentence tells you whether someone is measuring time exactly or speaking more loosely.
hint: Used to describe half of something.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 半: half

story: 双 refers to a pair or two matching things. 双手 means both hands. This makes it useful when speaking about things that naturally come together, such as hands, feet, or a pair of shoes.
hint: Used for pairs or both of something.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 双: pair; double

story: 单 can mean single or just one, in contrast with a pair or a group. 单人 describes something intended for one person. You may meet it when reading about rooms, beds, or individual activities.
hint: Used for single or individual items.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 单: single

story: 多 means many or much. In 多少, it pairs with 少, few or little, to ask how many or how much. You can use this question word when asking about a quantity or a price.
hint: Used to ask about quantity.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 多: many; much

story: 少 means few or little when read shǎo. 少量 means a small amount, often of something like food or a material. It makes a useful contrast with 多, meaning many or much.
hint: Used for small quantities.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 少: few; little

story: 今 refers to the present or current time. In 今天, it helps name today, the day we are in now. You also meet it in 今年, meaning this year.
hint: Used to refer to the present day.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 今: now; current

story: 明 can describe brightness, but it also appears in words about the next day or year. 明天 means tomorrow. Begin with this everyday word for the day that comes after today.
hint: Used to refer to the next day.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 明: bright; next

story: 昨 refers to the previous day or a recent past time, usually within a word. 昨天 means yesterday. Compare it with 今天, today, and 明天, tomorrow, to talk about three familiar days.
hint: Use 昨天 to talk about the day before today.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 昨: previous (day)

story: We are celebrating the arrival of this year with a big party. Everyone is happy because we have many goals to achieve together. It is a fresh start for us. In 今年 (jīn nián), the meaning is “this year.”
hint: Use 今年 to refer to the current calendar year.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 年: year

story: 岁 is used when giving someone’s age in years. 三岁 means three years old. It follows a number, helping you say how old a child or another person is.
hint: Use 岁 to describe a person's age in years.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 岁: year of age

story: The meeting will last for exactly one hour. Please make sure you arrive on time so we can finish early. Managing our schedule is very important for productivity. In 小时 (xiǎo shí), the meaning is “hour.”
hint: Use 小时 to measure a duration of sixty minutes.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 时: time; hour

story: 分 can mean to divide, and it also names a minute when talking about time. 分钟 means minute. You will often see it after a number when someone says how long an activity takes.
hint: Use 分钟 to talk about a specific minute duration.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 分: minute; divide

story: The race was incredibly close, decided by just one second. Every athlete trained hard to improve their speed. It is amazing how much can happen in such a short time. In 一秒 (yì miǎo), the meaning is “one second.”
hint: Use 秒 for the smallest unit of time here.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 秒: second (time)

story: 点 can mean a dot or a point, and it is also used when telling the time. 三点 means three o’clock. Put a number before 点 to begin naming the hours of the day.
hint: Use 点 to tell the time on a clock.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 点: dot; o’clock

story: The sun rises early in the morning during the summer. I like to drink coffee while watching the sky turn bright. It is the best time to start my day. In 早上 (zǎo shang), the meaning is “morning.”
hint: Use 早上 to refer to the early morning period.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 早: early; morning

story: We usually have dinner in the evening after work. The city lights look beautiful when it gets dark outside. It is a relaxing time to spend with my family. In 晚上 (wǎn shang), the meaning is “evening.”
hint: Use 晚上 to talk about the evening or night.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 晚: late; evening

story: I always take a short break at noon to eat lunch. It helps me stay focused for the rest of the day. I enjoy sitting in the park during this time. In 中午 (zhōng wǔ), the meaning is “noon.”
hint: Use 中午 to refer to the middle of the day.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 午: noon

story: The city lights shine brightly after the sun sets. People enjoy walking in the park during the cool evening air. In the example, 夜晚 refers to the nighttime period when most people are resting at home.
hint: Use this word to describe the time after sunset.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 夜: night

story: 周 can refer to a cycle, and in modern time expressions it means week. 周末 means weekend. You can recognize it when someone talks about plans for the end of the week.
hint: Refers to a seven-day cycle or a weekend.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 周: week; cycle

story: 期 refers to a period of time and appears in several time-related words. 星期 means week. Learn 星期 as a complete word before using it with numbers to name the days of the week.
hint: Used to denote a specific duration or week.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 期: period of time

story: The weather changes significantly as the year progresses through the calendar. I enjoy watching the leaves change color during the autumn months. In the example, 四季 refers to the four seasons of the year.
hint: Used to talk about the four seasons.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 季: season

story: 每 means every or each. 每天 means every day, making it useful for talking about regular habits. Reading, walking, or studying can all be activities that someone does 每天.
hint: Use this to indicate every instance or day.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 每: every

story: 次 counts how many times something happens. 一次 means one time or once. Use this pattern when talking about an action happening once, twice, or several times rather than counting physical objects.
hint: Use this to count how many times something happens.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 次: time; occurrence

story: 个 is a common measure word for counting many kinds of things. 三个 means three items when the thing is already understood. The spoken syllable often becomes light when it follows a number.
hint: A common word to count general objects.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 个: general measure word

story: 本 has several uses, including referring to a root or an origin. For beginners, it is especially useful when counting books: 一本书 means one book. 本 goes between the number and the word for book.
hint: Use this to count books or bound documents.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 本: book measure word; root

story: 张 is a measure word used when counting many flat things. 一张纸 means one sheet of paper. Notice the pattern: a number comes first, then 张, then the thing being counted.
hint: Use this to count flat objects like paper.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 张: measure word for flat things

story: 块 can refer to a piece or a chunk of something. In everyday speech about prices, it also means yuan. 一块钱 means one yuan, a useful phrase to recognize when shopping.
hint: Used for currency or chunks of items.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 块: piece; yuan (colloquial)

story: On this card, 只 is read zhī and counts certain animals. 一只猫 means one cat. The same character has another common reading, zhǐ, with a different meaning, so practise it together with this example.
hint: Use this word to count individual animals.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 只: measure word for some animals

story: 第 turns a number into an order or a position. 第一 means first, rather than simply one. You can use the same pattern to recognize second, third, and later positions in a list.
hint: Add this before numbers to show order.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 第: ordinal prefix

story: 先 tells you that something happens first or before something else. 先来 means to come first. It is useful when describing the order in which people arrive or things should be done.
hint: Use this to describe what happens before others.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 先: first; before

story: 再 often means again or then, for an action that follows or will happen later. In 再见, the complete expression means goodbye. Remember 再见 as the friendly phrase you say when leaving.
hint: Use this to indicate doing something once more.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 再: again; then

story: Here, 长 is read cháng and means long. In 长短, it pairs with 短, short, to talk about length. It has another reading, zhǎng, in other words, so connect this pronunciation with long things.
hint: Use this to describe something that is not short.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 长: long

story: 短 describes something short, especially its length or duration. 短发 means short hair. It makes a useful pair with 长, long, when comparing hair, clothing, or other things around you.
hint: Use this to describe something that is not long.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 短: short

story: When you are in a hurry to catch a bus, you move your feet quickly. This word describes high speed or urgency. For example, 快走 means to walk quickly.
hint: Use this to describe high speed.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 快: fast

story: When you are walking in a beautiful park, you might take your time. This word describes moving with little speed. For example, 慢走 means to walk slowly.
hint: Use this to describe low speed.
imageAlt: Ink-wash learning illustration for 慢: slow
